questions.q: How does Oracle Fusion track a change made to an already-approved purchase order?
options: It silently overwrites the original document with no history
It creates a new, numbered version of the purchase order, preserving the history of each change
It deletes the purchase order and requires a brand-new requisition
It only allows changes by contacting Oracle support directly
questions.explain: A change order produces a new version of the same purchase order, keeping a traceable history of what changed, by whom, and when.

questions.q: Which type of change is most likely to trigger a new approval cycle?
options: Fixing a typo in an internal text note
Changing the font used to print the purchase order
A change to quantity, price, or a line cancellation
Viewing the purchase order's change history
questions.explain: Significant financial changes like quantity, price, or cancellation are typically configured to require reapproval through the same approval engine.

questions.q: In the scenario where Meridian requests a unit price increase before shipping, what does Marcus do?
options: Cancels the purchase order and starts over with a new requisition
Updates the price directly on the invoice once it arrives, skipping the purchase order
Ignores the request since purchase orders cannot be changed after approval
Creates a change order updating the unit price, which routes back through approval before taking effect
questions.explain: A price change is applied through a change order, and because it is financially significant, it is routed back through approval before becoming effective.

questions.q: What is a retroactive change order?
options: A change applied to a purchase order after some downstream event, like a receipt, has already occurred, which can affect how that event's accounting is valued
A change order that can never be approved
A change order that only affects future purchase orders, never the current one
A mandatory change applied automatically every fiscal year
questions.explain: A retroactive change order is applied after a downstream event like a receipt already happened, which can affect that event's valuation and create later mismatches.

questions.q: Why should a consultant treat a retroactive change order with extra caution?
options: Because retroactive changes are illegal in Oracle Fusion Cloud
Because only requesters, not buyers, are allowed to create them
Because retroactive changes always cancel the purchase order automatically
Because it can create mismatches between what was received or invoiced and the purchase order's new terms, surfacing later as matching holds or reconciliation differences
questions.explain: Applying a change after goods were already received or invoiced can create inconsistencies that show up downstream as matching holds or accrual reconciliation issues.
